name: The Agent Economy payment rails
description: Alphabetical payment rail listings and the rules for the payment rail picker. Sponsor records and adoption figures are not match inputs.
attribution: The Agent Economy payment rails (https://theagenteconomy.si/data/payment-rails.json), licensed under CC BY 4.0.

questions.prompt: Can the rail take a 10 cent payment?

ordering: Candidates are listings in the payment rails category. Listings in other categories are left out.
Each answered question adds one match or zero. No preference and Any status add zero. One listing can gain at most one match from one question.
Merchant checkout matches the checkout tag, or a summary that contains the word merchant or the word checkout.
Agent to agent matches a summary that contains A2A.
An API matches the tag http-402, pay-per-call, or metering.
Cards, stablecoins, and Lightning match the tags cards, stablecoins, and lightning.
Spend limit matches the tag spend-limits.
An approval step matches a summary that contains an approval word or 2FA.
Spend limit or approval matches when either of those two checks match. The question still adds one match.

Per request matches the tag pay-per-call or metering, or a summary that contains per call, per API call, per payment, or per request. The tag http-402 alone does not match this question. Payment size is a separate question.

A 10 cent payment matches when a documented minimum is $0.10 or lower, or when one documented path is $0.10 or lower. A missing minimum, or a minimum that is not a single number, does not match. The match line also states the documented fee for $0.10. A USDC minimum is compared as the same number of dollars when the page states it beside a USD minimum and gives no rate.
Open source only matches an open_source value of true.
Live only matches a status of live.
The match list includes a listing only when it matches every answered question. A listing that misses an answer is left off that list and shown under Does not match, with the check it failed.
The order of the match list and the does not match list is alphabetical by listing name. With no answers set, every payment rail listing is in the match list in that same order.

The stored reason repeats that listing's summary, then names the tag, field, or summary word that matched. It adds no other claim. The page also shows one shorter line that names only the match, or only the failed check.
Adoption rows are copied from that listing's adoption block and add no matches. A row with no figure reads None published. If both sides have no figure, the block reads None published.
Sponsor records and sponsor payment links are not read.
Buyer region and compliance programs are not fields on these listings, so they are not questions.

The same answers are query parameters named pay, rail, control, micro, oss, status, and size. A GET request returns both lists in the HTML. The payment rails JSON file reads those same parameters and returns both lists.

micro.label: a per request charge
micro.note: Payment size is the size parameter. This per request check is not the price filter.

size.label: a 10 cent payment
size.note: Matches when a documented minimum allows $0.10. The line also states the documented fee.

predicates.match_rule: A listing is a match only when every answered question matches. Each answered question adds at most one match.

listings.name: Agent Vault
listings.summary: Self Labs product that gives an agent mock card and login tokens. A proxy checks the account holder's rules, then types the real value into the merchant page. The agent does not hold the card number.

fee_per_payment.text: Not documented as of 2026-11-09. What is Agent Vault does not state a fee per payment.

listings.name: Agentcard opencommerce
listings.summary: Commerce SDK that gives an agent one buy tool for catalog search, cart, checkout, and order tracking across online stores. The shopper approves each payment with a passkey on a link that lasts about 15 minutes, and Agentcard then places the order with the shopper's saved card.

fee_per_payment.text: The Open Commerce quickstart says Agentcard takes 1% of each live purchase. The fee is charged to a prefunded balance or to a saved card as the purchase completes. Fees too small to charge wait and are charged together with the next one.

minimum_payment.text: Not documented as of 2026-11-09. Commerce SDK quickstart does not state a minimum payment.

listings.name: Coinbase x402 Facilitator
listings.summary: Hosted x402 facilitator. A CDP API key authenticates the seller. It validates, screens payer and recipient, and settles on chain. Schemes are exact and upto, plus EVM batch settlement, on Base, Polygon, Arbitrum, Monad, World, and Solana. First 1,000 monthly on chain transactions are free, then $0.001. Verification is free.

fee_per_payment.text: The CDP Facilitator pricing table says the first 1,000 onchain transactions each month cost $0.00, and each onchain transaction above that costs $0.001. With exact, and with EVM upto, each accepted payment settles in one onchain transaction. The page says the fee is based on onchain activity, not on payment requests, and that payment verification is free.

listings.name: PayAI x402 facilitator
listings.summary: x402 facilitator whose Solana batch settlement guide calls facilitator support a public preview. USDC channels use signed vouchers off chain, then claims and distributions on chain. New channel deposits are 0.01 to 100 USDC. The public shared lane needs no account or API key.

fee_per_payment.text: The PayAI site says an account starts with 1,000 free credits, then $1 buys 1,000 credits. Each settled payment costs that network's rate in credits, usually a fraction of a cent. Rates refresh daily, testnets are free, and PayAI does not take a percentage of the payment amount.

minimum_payment.text: The PayAI site says there is no single advertised payment range that applies to every scheme and network. It says a customer price has to satisfy the asset's precision, the advertised requirements, and the selected scheme's rules.

listings.name: Polygon Agent CLI
listings.summary: Agent CLI with an embedded smart wallet. Session mode spends only inside an allowance the owner approves, x402 payments can be capped per call, and session logout revokes that install.

listings.name: px402
listings.summary: Privacy layer for x402 on Base from PRXVT. An agent funds a USDC reserve, withdraws blind signed coins, and a relayer sends plain USDC. The import replaces x402 wrapFetchWithPayment. The non-custodial reserve contract is on Base mainnet. The SDK uses PRXVT hosted issuer, registry, and facilitator services.

fee_per_payment.text: The px402 introduction says px402 charges 1% on each payment, paid on top of the price, and the merchant receives the price. The fee is rounded up to the smallest coin, $0.001, so every payment pays at least $0.001.

minimum_payment.text: Not documented as of 2026-11-09. What is px402 does not state a minimum payment.

matches.name: Circle Agent Wallets
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: Circle CLI wallet for agents. Spending policies cap USDC transfers per transaction and over a day, week, or month, and can allow or block recipient addresses. Policies apply to mainnet agent wallets.

matches.name: Circle Managed Agentic Payments
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: Seller side service on CPN Managed Payments. An agent pays USDC to a Circle sub-account, the platform unlocks the service, and Circle notifies the platform after unlock. Payouts cover 50+ local currencies. Agents pay via x402 or MPP. Eligible businesses contact Circle. Pricing is not documented as of 2026-11-09.

matches.name: Cloudflare Monetization Gateway
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: Closed beta since 2026-09-30. Seller rules charge APIs, MCP tools, sites, and datasets. Buyers and sellers must be in the United States. Fixed prices use exact and variable prices use upto, within the authorized maximum. Settlement uses the Coinbase x402 Facilitator in USDC on Base. Minimum settlement is $0.001.

matches.name: Coinbase Agentic Wallet
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: Coinbase wallet for agents. The Agentic Wallet CLI (awal) holds USDC and can send, trade, and pay x402 services under configurable caps per session and per transaction. Keys stay in Coinbase infrastructure. The MCP (npx @coinbase/payments-mcp) lets agents discover and pay for services only, and cannot send or trade.

matches.name: Coinbase Wallet MCP
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: Remote MCP server at wallet-mcp.coinbase.com. It connects an assistant to Coinbase Wallet, formerly Base App. Sends, swaps, signatures, batched calls, and x402 payments wait for approval in Coinbase Wallet.

matches.name: Coinbase x402 Facilitator
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: Hosted x402 facilitator. A CDP API key authenticates the seller. It validates, screens payer and recipient, and settles on chain. Schemes are exact and upto, plus EVM batch settlement, on Base, Polygon, Arbitrum, Monad, World, and Solana. First 1,000 monthly on chain transactions are free, then $0.001. Verification is free.

matches.name: Crossmint Agent Checkout
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: Hosted API that shops at a merchant for a user under a maximum amount. The caller sends a start URL and a task. Crossmint uses UCP, the merchant API, or a browser it runs, and may open a tracked affiliate link. The agent does not receive the card number.

matches.name: Fireblocks Agentic Payments Suite
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: A PSP white-labels the hosted x402 Gateway. Vaults run Policy Engine, pre-transfer KYT, and Travel Rule checks. Agent Wallets from Dynamic set scoped, revocable limits, merchant allowlists, time windows, and asset rules for x402 or MPP. The Apache 2.0 repository is the facilitator you run, not the hosted products.

matches.name: Hedera Agent Accounts
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: Owner funded spending account on Hedera. The owner sets a daily cap, a per transaction maximum, and a recipient allowlist in a smart contract, and can revoke the agent. Hedera says public testnet access is still forthcoming.

matches.name: KERNEL agent payments
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: KERNEL runs cloud browsers for agents. A vault lets an attached browser use a payment method without returning the credential. The agent fills checkout with aliases. At egress KERNEL checks the binding, then substitutes a one use credential or holds the request. The user approves. Merchants need no KERNEL integration.

matches.name: Kite Agent Passport
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: The agent pays x402 services from an allowance with no prompt, or from a session a passkey approves, with a per transaction limit, a total budget, and expiry, funded in USDC.e on Kite chain. The MiCA whitepaper says the chain is a Layer 1 built using Avalanche Layer 1 technology.

matches.name: L402
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: HTTP 402 flow that returns a bearer token, recommended as a macaroon, bound to a Lightning invoice by its payment hash. The client pays, then presents the preimage so the server can check payment without a lookup.

matches.name: Machine Payments Protocol
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: Open HTTP 402 protocol, co-authored by Stripe and Tempo, so an agent can authorize payment for an API with a card or a stablecoin and receive a receipt.

matches.name: Mastercard Agent Pay for Machines
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: Mastercard payment layer built on x402. An agent pays for metered services by signing a payment voucher after an HTTP 402 challenge, inside a spending limit set by its principal. Early Access opened on 2026-10-20 and is a pilot, not available commercially. Cloudflare Connect pilot settled on Base.

matches.name: Mercury MCP
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: Hosted MCP at https://mcp.mercury.com/mcp. An AI tool connects with OAuth and can request a payment to an existing recipient or a transfer between Mercury accounts. Those requests need approval in Mercury before money moves, and approval requests expire after approximately 5 minutes. Category and note edits apply immediately.

matches.name: MetaMask Agent Wallet
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: Agent wallet CLI for sending tokens and paying x402 requests. Guard Mode can enforce address and recipient allowlists and a rolling 24 hour outflow limit, and it asks for 2FA outside that policy.

matches.name: Natural Direct
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: Generally available as of 29 October 2026. An agent chooses ACH, a domestic wire, or realtime over RTP and FedNow for each payment from the same Natural wallet. A verified business with a funded wallet can use the API, SDKs, CLI, or payments MCP. Checks and international wires are coming soon.

matches.name: Nevermined
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: Payments facilitator that verifies and settles x402 and MPP charges against a payment plan, with metering and delegated card spending.

matches.name: PayAI x402 facilitator
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: x402 facilitator whose Solana batch settlement guide calls facilitator support a public preview. USDC channels use signed vouchers off chain, then claims and distributions on chain. New channel deposits are 0.01 to 100 USDC. The public shared lane needs no account or API key.

matches.name: Polygon Agent CLI
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: Agent CLI with an embedded smart wallet. Session mode spends only inside an allowance the owner approves, x402 payments can be capped per call, and session logout revokes that install.

matches.name: px402
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: Privacy layer for x402 on Base from PRXVT. An agent funds a USDC reserve, withdraws blind signed coins, and a relayer sends plain USDC. The import replaces x402 wrapFetchWithPayment. The non-custodial reserve contract is on Base mainnet. The SDK uses PRXVT hosted issuer, registry, and facilitator services.

matches.name: Rain Agent Vaults
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: A partner embeds an agent vault in its own app. The owner funds it by bank transfer, card, or stablecoins, and the agent pays or sends only what is in it. It pays with a scoped virtual card on Visa or Mastercard. Amount, merchant, and expiry are fixed at issuance.

matches.name: Shop MCP

matches.reason: Shopify MCP server and shop CLI. An agent searches Shopify Catalog, builds carts, and checks out with the buyer's Shop Pay. The buyer approves each purchase by default, or sets a weekly, monthly, or total budget. Off Shopify, an approved spend request returns a one time card.

matches.name: Skyfire
matches.line: No answer is set, so this listing is included in alphabetical order.
matches.reason: Issues signed KYAPay tokens that bind an agent identity to a payment the buyer has committed, which the seller charges after delivery.

Requests send privateKey and no bearer token. Mainnet is Arbitrum One, Base, and Ethereum, with an ETH protocol fee on transfers and withdrawals.

matches.reason: CLI for an agent to request a card purchase or a Machine Payments Protocol charge. Link returns a one time payment credential. Since 26 October 2026, a funded Link balance lets the agent skip approval for purchases under a per purchase limit the user sets, first in Instinct.

Who can obtain a card is not stated.
